details:
Space Fire Intelligent Platform is a dual-purpose, integrated web platform designed to advance space fire safety for both aerospace professionals and the general public. For scientists, researchers, and NASA personnel, it unifies scattered combustion research, historical incident archives, and microgravity experimental data into a single, accessible hub. Simultaneously, for students and space enthusiasts, it bridges the gap between complex aerospace engineering and accessible STEM education through simplified scientific insights, interactive gamification, and an intelligent AI guide named "Nor".

​The Challenge We Solve:

In microgravity environments, fire behaves unpredictably—lacking buoyancy-driven convection, smoke spreads rapidly through confined modules, blinding crews and blocking critical escape routes. Currently, two major gaps exist:

​1. For Researchers: Severe data fragmentation scatters vital lessons from historical incidents (such as the 1997 Mir space station solid-fuel oxygen generator fire) and raw experimental datasets (NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics - PSI) across complex, disconnected technical reports.

​2. For the Public & Students: Space combustion science is often locked behind dense, intimidating academic data, making it difficult for space enthusiasts to understand how fire behaves in space or why habitat safety protocols matter.

​Our Methodology & Research Effort:

​Human-Led Scientific Investigation: The most challenging part of building this platform was manually researching, verifying, and extracting exact physical parameters—specifically ambient pressure, temperature profiles, and oxygen (O_2) concentrations—from dense aerospace reports and experimental logs. Every piece of scientific data was gathered and validated directly by our team.

​AI-Assisted Data Structuring: Due to the massive volume and complexity of the collected data, we utilized AI strictly as an organizational tool to clean, structure, and format our manually researched datasets into a unified database—ensuring 100% human-verified scientific accuracy.

​Integrated Teamwork & Clear Communication: As a cohesive, interdisciplinary team, we divided responsibilities across deep scientific literature review, web development, and designing a clear, structured presentation that directly maps the core space-fire problems to our practical engineering solutions.

​Our Solution & Key Platform Capabilities:

​For Researchers & Aerospace Engineers (The Scientific Hub):

​1. Unified NASA PSI Repository: Brings NASA PSI experimental data together in one organized and accessible platform, alongside structured historical case studies (highlighting root causes like hydrocarbon contamination in life-support systems).

​2. Side-by-Side Experimental Comparison: Allows experts to compare different NASA experiments, materials, and environmental conditions (pressure, temperature, O_2 concentrations, and airflow velocities) side by side to evaluate terrestrial vs. microgravity flame spread behavior.

​3. "Nor" – AI-Powered Assistant: Integrates Nor, an intelligent assistant trained on validated aerospace safety literature and our structured datasets. Nor helps users navigate the platform, answers their questions in real time, explains experimental parameters, and enables researchers to rapidly query material flammability and mitigation protocols.

​4. Target Habitat Safety Guidelines: Provides practical design and operational recommendations for future long-duration space habitats (ISS, Lunar Gateway, and Mars missions).

​For Space Enthusiasts & General Users (Public Engagement & Learning):

5. Simplified Knowledge Hub: A dedicated, easy-to-navigate section tailored for non-specialists and curious learners, translating complex microgravity combustion physics and space fire history into bite-sized, engaging explanations without overwhelming raw datasets.

6. Interactive "Space Fire Safety" Quiz & Badge System: Features an engaging 10-question interactive quiz testing users' knowledge of fire behavior and safety in space. Users earn digital achievement shields based on their score ranges

for example, scoring 9 out of 10 or higher unlocks the prestigious "Space Safety Expert" shield.

​Current MVP & Future Vision:

While the current version of the website serves as a functional Minimum Viable Product (MVP) built within the hackathon's tight timeframe, our team has a clear roadmap for expansion. Given additional time and broader access to raw NASA experimental datasets, we plan to scale the platform with advanced real-time simulation models, expanded material databases, and deeper predictive analytics.

​Impact:

By combining rigorous human-led scientific research with smart data organization and public outreach through Nor, Space Fire Intelligent Platform eliminates research fragmentation for aerospace engineers while making space fire safety interactive and accessible for everyone.
